findings.issue: The text mentions direction and location but does not explicitly match accusative with direction and dative with location. The productive spatial frame should state that correspondence while retaining its qualification.
findings.original: With spatial ofer, direction and location help explain the two cases, but they are not an exceptionless rule for every use.
findings.proposed: With spatial ofer, the accusative commonly marks direction over or across a landmark, while the dative commonly marks location. This is a tendency, not an exceptionless rule for every use.
findings.evidence: U07-F-36-OFER: Fulk section 36, printed page 23 / one-based PDF page 35; coordinator reopened the registered image and checked the accusative/dative correspondence directly.
findings.scope_effect: Clarifies the already contracted frame; no new form, sense, construction or task is proposed.
findings.freeze_policy: Do not change the learner during pre-key solving. Reconcile this finding in phase 2 and record any revision before textual acceptance.
